caption: Supplementary Table S13. Complete postprocessed Dice comparison family
note: Note. All 30 planned postprocessed Dice contrasts are shown, complementing the significant-only Table S11. Positive differences favor the left model. Each contrast uses 252 intended frames from 18 patients within seed, 5,000 patient-cluster bootstrap resamples for BCa intervals, and 5,000 paired patient-level randomization draws. caption: Supplementary Table S19. Primary binary eye balanced accuracy by seed with patient-cluster BCa intervals
note: Note. Each held-out split contains 18 patients and 36 eyes. BCa intervals resample complete patients, preserving both eyes; they are seed-specific and are not intervals for the five-seed mean.

caption: Supplementary Table S20. Primary binary eye-level probability quality before and after calibration
note: Note. Values are arithmetic means ± sample SD across five overlapping holdouts, not confidence intervals; all entries use five valid seed estimates. Brier score, negative log-likelihood (NLL) and ten-bin equal-width expected calibration error (ECE) are conditional on evaluable eyes (30–36 of 36 intended eyes per model–seed unit). The positive category combines papilledema and pseudopapilledema. Temperatures were fitted on tuning data, not test outcomes. Lower values are preferable, but temperature scaling did not uniformly improve test probability quality; no significance test or equivalence claim is implied by this descriptive comparison. Raw and calibrated scores use the same evaluable population within a model–seed unit.

caption: Supplementary Table S21. Complementary binary eye-level discrimination and selective-risk endpoints
note: Note. Values are arithmetic means ± sample SD over five overlapping holdouts. MCC denotes the Matthews correlation coefficient, not the three-class task; AP is average precision. Both are conditional on evaluable eyes and use the operational temperature-scaled probabilities and locked threshold where applicable. They must not be interpreted as all-eye endpoints. Model-specific classifiers are primary; the Separately fitted ResNet-18 strategy is secondary and uses separately fitted classifiers for each ROI stream. AURC is the area-under-risk–coverage summary implemented as the arithmetic mean of cumulative error proportions over all 36 ranks. Ranking uses absolute distance from each locked threshold, with structural abstentions appended at lowest confidence as errors. Risk is ordinary misclassification risk, not 1 minus balanced accuracy. Lower AURC is preferable. These descriptive selective-risk results do not validate a new rejection policy or clinical benefit.
